title: Who stops weekly electronic symptom reporting during chemotherapy, and why: an explanatory sequential mixed methods evaluation
abstract: Objective: to describe completion of weekly electronic symptom reports and alert response in routine chemotherapy care, and to explain why patients stop reporting. Design: explanatory sequential mixed methods in two clinics of a regional cancer centre, March 2026 to May 2027. Methods: completion and alert timestamps for about 420 patients, a longitudinal model linking unanswered alerts to later completion, and interviews with patients who stopped and with triage nurses, integrated in a joint display. Results and conclusions will follow the analysis.
introduction: Randomised trials show that weekly electronic symptom reporting can reduce emergency visits when alerts are answered promptly, but in routine care many patients stop reporting within months. Why they stop, and how alert response contributes, has rarely been studied in the same patients.
methods: All patients offered weekly reporting in the breast and colorectal clinics are included. Completion over the first 12 weeks is the primary quantitative outcome; a mixed-effects model links unanswered severe alerts to completion the following week. Interviews with purposively sampled patients and triage nurses explore reasons, and a joint display integrates the strands.
results: No data have been analysed yet. The report will present completion by clinic, age, deprivation and language, alert response times by weekday and weekend, the mechanism model, the interview themes, and the joint display.
discussion: The discussion will relate the local patterns to the trial evidence, set out the changes to the response standard and the paper route before the remaining clinics start, and state what the evaluation cannot show about effectiveness.
limitations: Two clinics; confounding by illness severity; interview findings may not transfer to other tumour groups.
conclusion: To be written after integration; it will not claim that weekly reporting reduced emergency visits in this centre.
reportingChecklist: GRAMMS, with COREQ for the interview strand
summary: GRAMMS-structured draft with results left empty until analysis.
